newsitem.title: NORWAY: Preparations begin for Greenland oil exploration.
newsitem.headline: Preparations begin for Greenland oil exploration.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday a rig to measure water currents, pressure and temperatures had been moored 150 km (93 miles) west of the Greenland port of Nuuk in preparation for exploration drilling.

The unit, the first to be installed in the Fylla area, is moored in water 1,100 metres (3,600 ft) deep but will stop at about 300 metres below sea level to avoid damage from icebergs and ships. It will be in place for around six months, Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said.
An exploration and production licence was awarded to a consortium of Statoil, Phillips Petroleum, Denmark's Dopas and local company Nunaoil last December.
Covering 9,487 square km (3,663 sq miles), the Fylla acreage equals roughly 17 Norwegian North Sea blocks and is the first to be licensed off Greenland since the 1970s.
Seismic is due to be shot in the summer. Statoil said early surveys had identified interesting geological structures that could contain oil and gas.
